title: Finite canonical pullback carries the local germ formula to Theta
statement: Let f:X→Y be proper, Y locally Noetherian, F coherent, y∈Y and p,n≥0 [def-weil-proper-morphism,pqf-def-locnoeth,pqf-def-coherent]. Let r:formalFunctionsLocalCohomology(f,y,F,p)→H^p(X_n,F_n) be A-linear whose underlying function equals formalFunctionsFinitePullback [def-weil-pbc-formal-functions-finite-pullback]. For every A-linear a:formalFunctionsStalk(f,y,F,p)→formalFunctionsLocalCohomology(f,y,F,p) satisfying IsFormalFunctionsLocalComparison [def-weil-pbc-formal-functions-local-comparison], r composed with a satisfies IsFormalFunctionsTheta at level n [def-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-cohomology]. There is no quotient-system isomorphism in this statement.

source.place: Tag 02OD, finite-level identifications; Tags 089W, 01F7 and 01FB (read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02OD, /089W and /01FB)

proof.text: For arbitrary I,J,V,hy,D,xi choose K resolving F′; enough injectives exists on every scheme. Flatness of the canonical local spectrum map and base change gives local open choices E₀. Set E={E₀ with source:=D.source}; its psi, target and unit_square are unaffected, and the two germ representatives are now definitionally identical. No resolution-independence theorem is needed.

Obtain t and its two equations from the finite-open factorization. Apply ha to I,K,V,hy,E,xi. Apply t to that equality. Replace t∘restriction on the left by finite restriction∘formalFunctionsFinitePullback using the first factorization equation; the second gives the finite restricted pullback on the right. Use hr at the local class a(germ) to replace finitePullback by r; linear-map composition evaluates to r(a(germ)). This proves the defining Theta equality for every I,J,V,hy,D,xi.

proof_origin.place: Tag 02OD, proof: c_n factors through c; Tags 01F7 and 01FB: composition and restriction of cohomology h-maps (read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02OD and /01FB). X3: choose the same source resolution in local and finite open data; combine the two finite-open equations with ha and hr.
